C02: A governed profile MUST deny protected actions when policy or required identity/context is unavailable, and expose the denial posture.
A direct, managed, embedded or proxied tool request supplies forged tenant or actor facts, or policy loading fails
the protected effect does not occur and the caller receives a reason without hidden fallback.
Approval MUST bind issuer, action, resource, payload digest and authority revision; delayed execution MUST recheck current grants and limits.
A granted request waits while its grant is revoked or its payload changes
the old approval cannot authorize the changed or revoked effect.
C03: The definition pipeline MUST preserve required skill identity, version and configuration and reject unknown mandatory semantics.
A legacy or collaboration-profile definition is compiled, persisted, loaded and bound
its required semantics remain effective, or binding fails with field-level diagnostics.

Portable AgentDefinition, TeamDefinition, WorkflowDefinition and DeploymentBinding documents MUST NOT confer installed authority; private RepresentationGrant records MUST stay outside exported packages.
A definition claiming administrator or executive authority is imported or exported
installation requires independent trusted grants and exports contain neither those grants nor secrets.
C04: Clients MUST bind a run to a verified service instance and compatible capability profile, with credential references rather than embedded credentials.
A user selects between two UAR instances or selects an instance missing a mandatory feature
new work uses the selected compatible instance or refuses admission with a specific diagnostic.
Only the registered lifecycle owner MAY stop or replace a managed service; clients MUST distinguish reattachment from new-session placement and migration.
A nonowner client closes while a remote service has active runs
the service keeps running; reconnect preserves the native run identity without silently creating a replacement.
C05: Full-run delegation MUST be distinct from model-provider bridging; a delegated run MUST have exactly one tool/token-loop executor.
BossFang chooses native execution, UAR provider access or full UAR delegation
the observable execution trace identifies which runtime owns the loop and BossFang does not replay delegated tools.
Delegated run control MUST preserve native IDs and reconcile uncertain admission before retries; cancellation and detachment MUST have distinct semantics.
An admission response is lost and the caller reconnects, then cancels the recovered task
lookup returns the existing task or a truthful unresolved state; cancellation reaches its executor and no duplicate effect is launched.
C06: Request execution, on-demand instances and resident instances MUST expose distinct lifetimes; durable state MUST NOT depend on a permanently active model loop.
Two users instantiate the same definition and one activation passivates or crashes
their state remains isolated and admitted work resumes from the correct instance state on activation.
Instances MUST serialize mutating turns, bound queue/restart/retention policies, and reject stale ownership while keeping administrative cancellation responsive.
An old activation returns after replacement while a current tool call is blocked
the stale activation cannot commit and authorized cancellation/status control remains available.
C07: Each observer MUST have its own authorized source-agent/conversation intersection, projection, delivery cursor and acknowledgement.
Two observers subscribe to overlapping conversations but have different access grants
each receives its own permitted projection and neither receives unauthorized conversation content.
Committed event publication and observer admission MUST recover from interruptions with stable occurrence identity; queued content MUST be checked against current authority.
The source or observer crashes at publication, admission or acknowledgement, and a subscription is revoked before recovery
recoverable authorized work resumes without silent gaps; revoked queued content is withheld and any retention gap is visible.
C08: Channel routes MUST bind provider/account/workspace/room/thread/sender and chosen recipient, with explicit handler precedence and observer-copy rights.
A channel message matches two handlers and two observer subscriptions, then the bridge restarts
the declared conflict rule determines the handler and only authorized observers receive independent copies; affinity remains stable.
Forwarded events MUST preserve source occurrence and separate disclosure, delivery, execution and reply permissions; reaction depth, fanout and duplicate effects MUST be bounded.
An agent reply echoes through the channel into an A-B-A observer chain or a queued grant is revoked
duplicate effects and unauthorized replies are blocked, causal budgets terminate the loop, and queued revoked content is withheld.
C09: Teams MUST record versioned membership, task inputs/outputs/dependencies and atomic claims; child authority MUST be no broader than its delegated grant.
Two workers claim one task revision and an old worker returns after reassignment
only one current claim can complete or authorize effects and the stale result remains nonauthoritative evidence.
Teams MUST enforce aggregate budgets, scoped memory/artifacts and independent reviewer authority with explicit parent and peer lifetime rules.
A member is removed or a parent is cancelled while workers spend from the shared budget
new effects from revoked workers are denied, aggregate reservations cannot overspend, and unrelated authorized peers retain their declared lifetime.
C10: A feedback workflow MUST support draft-only operation and scoped standing authorization for sanitized issue creation, with durable effect identity and uncertainty reconciliation.
The same authorized feedback arrives by direct API and BossFang channel, and an issue-creation response is lost
reconciliation produces one issue or a visible unresolved outcome without blind retry; no customer message or roadmap promise is implied.
Connector capabilities MUST separately authorize reading, drafting, writing, sending and publishing; external content MUST be treated as data.
A Slack, Notion, Jira or GitHub item instructs the agent to expand its rights or disclose unrelated content
the instruction cannot expand authority, and only explicitly permitted targets and actions execute.
C11: Forge business writes MUST remain server-authoritative; read projections MUST disclose freshness and permission scope separately from personal peer documents.
An offline client views stale data and submits a business write against a changed version
the view reports freshness and the server accepts, rejects or conflicts the command through the authoritative API.
Offline business commands MUST retain stable identity and expose queued, accepted, rejected, conflicted or uncertain outcomes without treating transport acknowledgement as acceptance.
A command is resent after reconnect or its response is lost
the client reconciles one authoritative outcome or a visible uncertain state, without duplicate business effects.
C12: KnowMe personal documents MUST preserve authorized peer synchronization and explicit home/cloud participation, with schema compatibility and recovery policy.
A permitted device reconnects after offline edits while a different peer lacks permission
authorized compatible data converges according to document policy and the unauthorized peer receives no new disclosure.
Consent and data-use boundaries MUST be enforced for new synchronization and agent access; offline validity limits and residual downloaded copies MUST be disclosed.
Sharing is revoked or device credentials are rotated while another peer remains offline
new online access is denied and offline behavior follows the declared bounded policy; the system does not claim remote erasure of already downloaded copies.
C13: UAR deployment profiles MUST declare supported embedding, storage, tools and governance capabilities independently of BossFang, Gate, Fabric or The Boss availability.
A mobile or embedded host lacks a required sandbox, tool or governance facility
the affected capability refuses admission or uses an explicitly selected constrained profile without silently expanding authority.
Mobile suspension and home/cloud disconnection MUST have explicit queue, retention and resumption semantics; a device MUST NOT promise perpetual background residency.
The mobile process is suspended while an observer or remote workflow has admitted work
durable work is resumed or a documented gap is surfaced; selecting a new host does not silently migrate the existing session.
C14: The Boss MUST expose effective runtime binding, ownership, policy posture, lifecycle, budget, approvals and subscription state across local and remote instances.
An operator connects two runtimes and an externally managed BossFang service
the UI identifies each instance and permits only authorized controls without conflating product history with runtime checkpoints.
BossFang channel administration MUST remain in its isolated authenticated console surface; embedding MUST preserve origin, credential and navigation boundaries.
A console redirects, attempts privileged host operations or targets an untrusted origin
the host does not disclose credentials or grant ambient mini-app privileges and offers a controlled failure path.
C15: The skill family MUST preserve supported native configuration and explicitly diagnose required unsupported options across UAR, Codex, Claude Code, Copilot, Kimi Code, MiniMax CLI, OpenCode and DeepSeek Harness.
A team with a required native feature is exported to a harness without that feature
export fails with a capability diagnostic instead of silently dropping semantics or claiming equivalent plugin/team support.
Guided team creation MUST discover model capabilities/cost classes and bind reviewed skills; handoffs MUST record source revision, artifacts, authority and selected memory references.
A coding task transfers between supported harnesses
the receiver verifies the checkpoint and available capabilities before work; private memory is not copied wholesale, and full/mini helpers use the declared Node.js/TypeScript 7 toolchain.
C16: Team creation MUST explain the smallest useful role set, a single-agent alternative, skill choices, output contracts and model/cost tradeoffs.
An inexperienced user requests a coding, marketing, product or full-design task
the guide proposes accountable roles and reviewed skills with separate evaluator assignments and explicit write limits.

UI/UX, mobile, security, product, documentation and code-review roles MUST have explicit evidence and action scopes; titles MUST NOT grant publication, communication or compliance certification authority.
A security or product specialist recommends an external action
the resulting artifact distinguishes advice from verified evidence and the action follows the separate governing grant.
C17: Executive assistance MUST distinguish role assistance, simulation, disclosed human representation and delegated organizational action through separate trusted grants.
A human authorizes a personal twin but the organization has not granted spending authority
the twin may perform permitted personal representation and cannot spend organizational funds.
Offboarding, expiry and revocation MUST block new protected access/effects; a simulated human approval MUST NOT satisfy a required real-human decision.
An offboarded executive twin attempts an action or generates a simulated approval
the effect is denied and the audit records the governing grant state and unmet real-human requirement.
C18: A release MUST advertise only deployment/protocol/schema/policy combinations that passed the operational-mode scenarios on identified builds and hosts.
A new combination is requested without interoperability or recovery evidence
it remains unsupported or explicitly experimental with required features disabled; success on a unit suite cannot certify the combination.
Automatic cross-host takeover MUST remain disabled until state and effect fencing are demonstrated; release evidence MUST distinguish quality, cost, recovery and unknown outcomes.
Two hosts can believe they own a recovering run or an external effect has uncertain completion
stale authority cannot commit and recovery reconciles uncertainty without promising exactly-once effects.
